versions.notes: Second Multi-Pilot alpha. USB networking now stays up under sustained load: two bugs in the USB driver Arduino ships, one that stalled sending and one that made the gate drop its USB address, are fixed, and the gate ran 30 minutes at full load and 20 RotorHazard races over USB without a failure. Also fixes a web server hang when a page load and the LED animation drew the LEDs together. Adds firmware support for RotorHazard plugin 2 (every pilot, live RSSI, frequencies set from RotorHazard; the plugin itself follows separately) and a new Waveshare ESP32-S3-ETH build with wired Ethernet. The Waveshare build is UNTESTED: it has never been run on the board and may not boot or connect, so only flash it if you are happy to test it. Tested for this release: a Seeed XIAO ESP32S3 with an ESP32-C5 over USB; the other board builds share the same code but were not run on hardware. Everything from Multi-Alpha-1 is included. Devices on Multi-Alpha-1, 1.8.3 or the 1.8 release candidates can update over the air; the Waveshare board needs a USB flash the first time.

First Multi-Pilot alpha for testing with an ESP32-C5 receiver running FPVGate C5MK firmware version 2 or later. Supports up to eight pilots, individual calibration, race results, SD RSSI recording and per-pilot Visual Marshal editing. Keep the web race page open for race completion and browser announcements. Physical eight-pilot testing is still outstanding. Builds are provided for the AIO, Solo, Seeed XIAO ESP32S3, ESP32-S3 DevKitC-1 and XIAO ESP32S3 Plus. The C5 receiver needs separate firmware. Upgrading from 1.7.x requires a full USB flash; existing 1.7.3 SD cards need no changes.

Release candidate for the FPVGate AIO and Seeed XIAO ESP32S3 only. Other boards should stay on rc-2.

Fixes battery monitoring on the Seeed XIAO ESP32S3, which was reading a pin with no ADC and reporting a meaningless voltage. It now reads D0, which needs an external 100K/100K divider from the battery, as the XIAO has none onboard.

Installing this over a cable is still required if you are coming from 1.7.3 or earlier: the partition table changes and an over-the-air update cannot migrate to it.

Release candidate. Adds gzipped web assets, which cut a cold page load from about 7 seconds to 2 and fixed the interface failing to load when a browser opened several connections at once. Also carries everything from the betas: USB networking (the gate is reachable at 192.168.7.1 over USB-C), over-the-air updates from the device interface, the visual marshal and the merged race editor.

Installing this over a cable is still required if you are coming from 1.7.3 or earlier: the partition table changes and an over-the-air update cannot migrate to it.

USB networking works on Windows and Linux. macOS is not supported, as it has no RNDIS driver.

Adds over-the-air updates from the device web interface, so future updates no longer need a cable. Also USB networking on the AIO, the visual marshal, and a larger filesystem partition.

Installing this over a cable is still required if you are coming from 1.7.3 or earlier: the partition table changes and an over-the-air update cannot migrate to it.

USB networking on the AIO, visual marshal with SD RSSI capture, and a larger filesystem partition. Requires a full wire flash: the partition table changes, so an over-the-air update cannot migrate to it.
